headline: California's new "No Robo Bosses Act" stops employers from letting AI alone decide to discipline or fire workers.
score_reason: Lowered by two: the law was signed in late September 2026 (coverage dated 30 Sep), so this is a later explainer, not new news.
importance_line: California workers gain a right to human review and an explanation of AI-driven firings from 1 July 2027, but a lawyer expects employers to look for loopholes, and other states have chosen disclosure rules instead.
summary: ZDNET reports that California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed SB 947, the "No Robo Bosses Act", which bars employers from leaving discipline and firing decisions entirely to AI and requires them to check the output and give the employee the reasons. The law takes effect on 1 July 2027 and lets workers complain to the state Labor Commissioner; it was signed in late September 2026, so this is an explainer of earlier news.
notes: Signing date taken from earlier coverage headlines (CNBC 30 Sep 2026); ZDNET gives none. Category LAW (new state law) instead of SOC default.
